meta.title: Renewable and conventional electricity compared
meta.units: capacity factor as a fraction; installed cost US$/kW; LCOE US$/kWh; land use m² per MWh/yr; lifecycle emissions gCO2e/kWh; generation TWh
meta.description: Capacity factor, installed cost, levelized cost of energy (LCOE), land use, lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions and growth for eleven electricity sources. Each number carries its own unit, year and source id.
meta.license: Compilation CC BY 4.0. Figures are facts reported by the cited sources; OWID/Ember data CC BY 4.0.

series.central: Global weighted average for projects commissioned in 2024 (IRENA). For land use: median of plant-level studies (Lovering et al. 2022). For emissions: median of lifecycle studies (IPCC AR5).
series.range: Range assumed for new US plants (Lazard LCOE+ 2025). For emissions: min–max of lifecycle studies (IPCC AR5).
series.us: United States: 2024 fleet average capacity factor (EIA Electric Power Annual) or AEO2026 overnight cost of a new plant (EIA).
series.direct: Direct footprint only (pads, roads, plant, wells), where the study separates it.

definitions.cf: Capacity factor: energy produced in a year divided by nameplate capacity × 8,760 hours. IRENA figures are for new projects commissioned in 2024; EIA figures are what the whole existing US fleet achieved in 2024, including plants that were curtailed or ran part-time.
definitions.capex: Total installed cost (IRENA) or total capital cost (Lazard): everything needed to build the plant, per kW of capacity. EIA overnight cost excludes interest during construction. IRENA and Lazard are 2024 and 2025 US dollars; EIA AEO2026 is 2025 dollars.
definitions.lcoe: Levelized cost of energy: the constant price per kWh that repays building, running, fuel and financing over the plant’s life. No subsidies. Excludes grid connection beyond the site, backup, storage and other system-integration costs, and the cost of pollution.
definitions.land: Land-use intensity, Lovering et al. 2022: area occupied (direct plus indirect, e.g. mines and gas fields) per unit of electricity generated each year, converted from ha/TWh/y (× 0.01). Rooftop solar and offshore wind are not in the study’s table and are left blank.
definitions.ghg: Lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions per kWh: building, fuel supply, operation and decommissioning, in CO2-equivalent, including albedo effects, from IPCC AR5 WGIII Annex III Table A.III.2 (2014). Newer studies (UNECE 2021, NREL 2021 update) report broadly similar medians.
definitions.growth: World generation from the matching OWID/Ember series: solar includes utility, rooftop and CSP; wind includes onshore and offshore; geothermal is “other renewables” (mostly geothermal, plus tidal and wave).

caveats: IRENA, Lazard and EIA use different methods, years, regions and costs of capital. Do not read a dot against a bar from another source as a like-for-like comparison.

IRENA computes LCOE project by project with country-specific costs of capital (3.8 % in Europe to 12 % in Africa for 2024) and then averages; the average of many LCOEs is not the LCOE of average inputs.
Lazard’s ranges are for new US plants with 60 % debt at 8 % and 40 % equity at 12 %; IRENA’s are global. Lazard’s nuclear figure is based on Vogtle costs.
LCOE ignores when the energy arrives. A kWh from a variable source at noon is worth less to a grid than a kWh available on demand.
Lifetimes marked as this page’s assumption are not taken from a source.
